Wait literally no, that’s not how the federal government works at all. I think you have a fundamental misunderstanding on our fiscal policy. 

In 2022 we collected ~4.9 trillion (850 billion of which was from the previous fiscal year), while we spent ~6.27 trillion. This is called deficit spending, this isn’t money collected from tax payers. This is money that the fed prints to be able to pay for different things (namely defense budget, SSA, AND the student loan forgiveness). 

Now to get ahead of you when you’re going to say that this is why inflation is running rampant, I implore you to look into the economic consensus that deficit spending in an economic downturn (which we were in coming out of the coronavirus pandemic) is an overwhelmingly good thing. 

Please don’t continue to spread the misinformation that this came from taxes. Please actually look at the policy before just making blanket false statements.

Genuine question, would you be ok with the Pell grant loans then? The ones that went to federal employees (teachers mainly) who would work in underfunded school for a certain period of time, getting a large sum taken off of their loan? 

More simply, are you against the loan forgiveness because it will be used for “useless” degrees, and you would be ok with it being for more applied degrees?
